title: Sleep and Hormones
content: Hormone changes affect sleep architecture. The drop in estrogen and progesterone before menstruation can lead to poorer sleep quality, trouble falling asleep, or waking up frequently. Progesterone has a slight sleep-inducing effect, but its sudden drop can increase wakefulness. Maintaining good sleep hygiene and managing stress (which lowers cortisol) can help improve sleep quality during the luteal phase.
